source_text: Οἱ μὲν τοὺς ἐγκωμιαστικοὺς λόγους τοῖς πλουσίοις δωροφοροῦντες οὐ μόνον κόλακες καὶ ἀνελεύθεροι δικαίως ἂν ἔμοιγε κρίνεσθαι δοκοῖεν, ὡς ἐπὶ πολλῷ προσποιούμενοι χαρίσασθαι τὰ ἀχάριστα. ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσεβεῖς καὶ ἐπίβουλοι· ἀσεβεῖς μὲν, ὅτι παρέντες αἰνεῖν καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν μόνον τέλειον καὶ ἀγαθὸν θεόν, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ εἰς ὃν τὰ πάντα, περιάπτουσι το . . . . . . . . . . . τὸ γέρας ἀνθρώποις ἐνασ . . . . . . . . . . . βίῳ κυλινδουμένοις. . . . . . . τὸ κεφάλαιον ὑποκείμενον τῇ κρίσει τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐπίβουλοι δέ, ὅτι καὶ αὐτῆς τῆς περιουσίας καθ᾿ αὑτὴν ἱκανῆς οὔσης χαυνῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν κεκτημένων καὶ διαφθεῖραι καὶ ἀποστῆσαι τῆς ὁδοῦ, δι᾿ ἧς ἐπιτυχεῖν ἔστι σωτηρίας, οἳ δὲ προσεκπλήσσουσι τὰς γνώμας τῶν πλουσίων ταῖς ἡδοναῖς τῶν ἀμέτρων ἐπαίνων ἐπαίροντες καὶ καθάπαξ τῶν ὅλων πραγμάτων πλὴν τοῦ πλούτου, δι᾿ ὃν θαυμάζονται. παρασκευάζοντες ὑπερφρονεῖν, τὸ δὴ τοῦ λόγου πῦρ ἐπὶ πῦρ μετοχετεύοντες, τύφῳ τῦφον ἐπαντλοῦντες καὶ ὄγκον πλούτῳ προσανατιθέντες βαρεῖ φύσει φορτίον βαρύτερον, οὗ μᾶλλον ἐχρῆν ἀφαιρεῖν καὶ περικόπτειν, ὡς σφαλεροῦ νοσήματος καὶ θανατηφόρου· τῷ γὰρ ὑψουμένῳ καὶ μεγαλυνομένῳ παραπέπηγεν ἀντίστροφος ἡ πρὸς τὸ ταπεινὸν μεταβολὴ καὶ πτῶσις, ὡς ὁ θεῖος διδάσκει λόγος. ἐμοὶ δὲ φαίνεται μακρῷ φιλανθρωπότερον εἶναι τοῦ θεραπεύειν. . . . . . . . . . . . τοὺς πλουτοῦντας . . . . . . . . . . ἐπὶ κακῷ τὸ συναίρεσθαι . . . . . . . . . . τὴν σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ἅπαντα τὸν δυνατὸν τρόπον, τοῦτο μὲν ἐξαιτουμένους παρὰ θεοῦ τοῦ βεβαίως καὶ ἡδέως τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ τέκνοις τὰ τοιαῦτα προϊεμένου, τοῦτο δὲ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ σωτῆρος ἰωμένους τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, φωτίζοντας καὶ προσάγοντας ἐπὶ τὴν τῆς ἀληθείας κτῆσιν, ἧς ὁ τυχὼν καὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς ἐλλαμπρυνόμενος μόνος τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ἀναιρήσεται. δεῖται δὲ καὶ ἡ εὐχὴ ψυχῆς εὐρώστου καὶ λιπαροῦς ἄχρι τῆς ἐσχάτης ἡμέρας τοῦ βίου συμμεμετρημένης καὶ ἡ πολιτεία διαθέσεως χρηστῆς καὶ μονίμου καὶ πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς τοῦ σωτῆρος ἐπεκτεινομένης.
orientation: Clement opens his homily by condemning those who flatter the rich, before turning to the question of how the rich can be saved.
pass_a_gloss: Those who bring encomiastic speeches as gifts to rich persons, not only flatterers and illiberal would they rightly, to me at least, seem to be judged, as pretending to bestow as a great favor things that are thankless. But also impious and treacherous: impious, because, having neglected to praise and glorify the only perfect and good God, from whom are all things and through whom are all things and unto whom are all things, they attach the prize to men wallowing in a life subject to judgment, the chief point lying under the judgment of God; treacherous, because, although wealth itself by itself is sufficient to puff up the souls of those who possess it and to corrupt and to lead away from the way through which it is possible to attain salvation, they further terrify the minds of rich persons, exalting them with the pleasures of immoderate praises and making them despise absolutely all things except wealth, on account of which they are admired, pouring fire upon fire, as the saying goes, drawing off pride upon pride and adding to wealth, heavy by nature, a heavier burden, from which rather it was necessary to take away and cut off, as a dangerous and deadly disease; for to the one who is exalted and magnified there is fixed, as a counterpart, the change to the lowly and a fall, as the divine word teaches. But to me it seems far more humane than to flatter to help the rich toward salvation in every possible way, on the one hand asking from God, who surely and gladly bestows such things upon his own children, on the other hand healing their souls by word through the grace of the Savior, enlightening and leading them to the acquisition of the truth, of which the one who obtains it and is made bright by good works alone will carry off the prize of eternal life. And prayer needs a soul that is vigorous and rich, measured out to the last day of life, and the way of life needs a disposition that is good and steadfast and stretched out toward all the commandments of the Savior.

lemmas.gloss: pouring from one channel to another

choices.why: The verb means to present as a gift; rendering it as a participle preserves the ongoing action of the flatterers.
The term means servile or unworthy of a free person; 'illiberal' keeps the ethical force Clement intends.
The verb means to make loose or flabby, metaphorically to make vain or conceited; 'puff up' captures the moral corruption.
The compound adds intensity to striking or astounding; 'further terrify' shows the added harm beyond wealth's own effect.

choices.english: pouring from one channel to another
choices.why: The verb means to divert a stream; the image is of transferring fire to fire, so the rendering keeps the metaphor of channeling.
The verb means to stretch oneself toward something; the rendering keeps the active, ongoing orientation toward the commandments.

bible_refs.note: ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ εἰς ὃν τὰ πάντα
τῷ γὰρ ὑψουμένῳ καὶ μεγαλυνομένῳ παραπέπηγεν ἀντίστροφος ἡ πρὸς τὸ ταπεινὸν μεταβολὴ καὶ πτῶσις

pass_b_english: Those who bring speeches of praise as gifts to rich people seem to me to deserve to be judged not only flatterers and illiberal, since they pretend to bestow as a favor what is actually thankless. They are also impious and treacherous. They are impious because they pass over praising and glorifying the only perfect and good God, from whom are all things and through whom are all things and to whom are all things, and they attach the prize to human beings who wallow in a life that is subject in its entirety to the judgment of God. They are treacherous because wealth by itself is enough to puff up the souls of those who possess it, to corrupt them, and to turn them away from the road by which salvation can be attained. Yet these people further indulge the appetites of the rich with the pleasures of immoderate praise, exalting them and making them despise everything in the whole world except wealth, the very thing for which they are admired. As the saying goes, they pour fire upon fire, drawing off conceit and pouring it upon conceit, and they add to wealth a burden heavier than its naturally heavy load. What they ought to do is take away from it and cut it off all around, as one would with a dangerous and deadly disease. For to the one who is lifted up and magnified, the opposite change is fixed in place: humiliation and fall, as the divine word teaches.

To me it seems far more humane to heal the rich for their salvation in every possible way, asking this from God, who surely and gladly grants such things to his own children, and healing their souls by the word through the grace of the Savior, enlightening them and leading them to the acquisition of the truth. The one who obtains this truth and is made bright by good works alone will carry off the prize of eternal life. Prayer requires a soul that is vigorous and persistent, measured out to the last day of life, and a way of life requires a disposition that is good and steadfast and stretched out toward all the commandments of the Savior.
notes: The source text contains several lacunae marked by dots, especially in the first half; the gloss renders only the legible words and does not supply missing text.

problems.quote: far more humane than flattering the rich to work together with them for their salvation
problems.why: Greek says it is more charitable to heal the rich, not to flatter them; meaning and agency are changed.
problems.fix: to me it seems far more charitable to heal the rich

problems.why: The source does not cite Proverbs 16:18; the reference is added erroneously.

problems.quote: who wallow in a life of sin, the very thing that lies under the judgment of God
problems.source_quote: ἐνασ . . . . . . . . . . . βίῳ κυλινομένοις. . . . . . . τὸ κεφάλαιον ὑποκείμενον τῇ κρίσει τοῦ θεοῦ
problems.why: The lacuna obscures whether 'sin' is in the source; 'the very thing' (τὸ κεφάλαιον) likely refers to the prize, not life.
problems.fix: who wallow in a life . . . the sum total that lies under the judgment of God
problems.ruling: Greek fragment lacks 'sin'; translator adds it and misreads τὸ κεφάλαιον as 'the very thing' rather than 'prize'.

problems.source_quote: ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ δι᾿ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ εἰς ὃν τὰ πάντα
problems.why: The source does not cite Romans 11:36; the reference is unsupported.
problems.ruling: Source has no scripture citation; 'ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα...' is unmarked. Adding '(Romans 11:36)' misleads reader into thinking it's in the source text.

edits.old: far more humane than flattering the rich to work together with them for their salvation
edits.new: far more humane to heal the rich for their salvation

edits.old: and attach the prize to human beings who wallow in a life of sin, the very thing that lies under the judgment of God.
edits.new: and attach the prize to human beings who wallow in a life . . . the sum total that lies under the judgment of God.

edits.old: humiliation and fall, as the divine word teaches (Proverbs 16:18).
edits.new: humiliation and fall, as the divine word teaches.

fixed: Changed 'far more humane than flattering the rich to work together with them for their salvation' to 'far more humane to heal the rich for their salvation' because the source says 'τοῦ θεραπεύειν' (to heal), not 'to flatter'.

Changed 'who wallow in a life of sin, the very thing that lies under the judgment of God' to 'who wallow in a life . . . the sum total that lies under the judgment of God' because the source has a lacuna and 'τὸ κεφάλαιον' refers to the sum total, not 'the very thing'.
Removed '(Proverbs 16:18)' because the source does not cite Proverbs 16:18.
Removed '(Romans 11:36)' because the source does not cite Romans 11:36.

problems.quote: Terrify the minds of the rich with the pleasures of immoderate praise
problems.source_quote: οἳ δὲ προσεκπλήσσουσι τὰς γνώμας τῶν πλουσίων ταῖς ἡδοναῖς τῶν ἀμέτρων ἐπαίνων ἐπαίροντες
problems.why: Greek says they indulge the appetites of the rich; English adds ‘terrify’, changing the action and tone.
problems.fix: Indulge the appetites of the rich with the pleasures of immoderate praise
problems.ruling: προσεκπλήσσουσι means 'fill up/stuff' not 'terrify'; ἡδοναῖς are pleasures of praise, indulging not frightening.

edits.old: Yet these people further terrify the minds of the rich with the pleasures of immoderate praise
edits.new: Yet these people further indulge the appetites of the rich with the pleasures of immoderate praise

fixed: Agency: Greek προσεκπλήσσουσι means 'strike with amazement' or 'astound', not 'terrify'; the English 'terrify' misstates the source. Changed to 'indulge the appetites' to match the sense of overwhelming the rich with flattering pleasures.

last_rejected.quote: puff up the souls of those who possess it
last_rejected.why: Greek says to corrupt the souls, not to puff them up with pride.
last_rejected.fix: corrupt the souls of those who possess it
last_rejected.ruling: χαυνῶσαι means to puff up/relax/dissolve; corrupt is διαφθεῖραι, listed separately next in the Greek.

last_rejected.quote: impious, because they pass over praising and glorifying the only perfect and good God
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀσεβεῖς μὲν, ὅτι παρέντες αἰνεῖν καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν μόνον τέλειον καὶ ἀγαθὸν θεόν
last_rejected.why: Greek says they are impious because they *praise* God, not because they pass over praising.
last_rejected.fix: impious, because they, being present, praise and glorify the only perfect and good God
last_rejected.ruling: παρέντες means passing over/neglecting; the infinitives αἰνεῖν καὶ δοξάζειν are objects of παρέντες.

last_rejected.quote: since they pretend to bestow as a favor what is actually thankless
last_rejected.why: The Greek passage contains no such clause; it adds meaning not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the clause or replace with a faithful rendering of the Greek text.
last_rejected.ruling: Source has προσποιούμενοι χαρίσασθαι τὰ ἀχάριστα: pretending to bestow (χαρίσασθαι) what is thankless (ἀχάριστα).

polish.changed: Repaired the garbled sentence about human beings under God's judgment by completing the thought naturally, clarified the structure of the two accusations against flatterers, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: wallow in a life . . . the sum total that lies under the judgment of God
notes.why: Ellipsis breaks the sentence; meaning is lost.
notes.fix: Supply the missing text or note the lacuna.
